sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Gold miners (BRMS, NEM, SGER) benefit durably from central-bank reserve diversification and a weakening USD, sustaining premium valuations regardless of short-term rate cuts.
Nickel and battery-metal players (MBMA, AMMN) are structurally supported by Indonesia's ban on raw ore exports and the global EV supply chain's pivot to high-pressure acid leach processing.
Coal equities (COAL, PSAB) face a durable regulatory overhang from domestic market obligations and carbon transition policies, capping long-term multiples despite short-term price rallies.
sectors.ai: Buy selectively into gold and nickel names riding the IDX momentum, prioritizing MBMA, BRMS, and AMMN for near-term upside as global precious-metal prices firm and Indonesia's downstream policy tailwind persists. Trim coal exposure (COAL) despite the bounce, as thermal demand softens into Q4. Watch ALKA and PSAB for speculative retail-driven spikes—take profits on any further 10%+ runs.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US solar equipment makers (SEDG, ENPH) are re-rating on IRA clarity and grid-scale backlog, a durable driver independent of rate cuts.
Indonesia's VKTR rides the national EV-bus conversion mandate (e-bus fleet targets by 2030), a structural policy tailwind with local-content protection.
Power generators (NRG, CEG) benefit from AI data-center demand, but their upside is capped by fuel-cost volatility and regulatory caps, making them tactical, not core.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in US solar names (SEDG, ENPH) and Indonesia EV-bus pure-play VKTR; momentum is broad and signal remains NORMAL, so add on dips rather than chase. Trim NRG/CEG into strength—their utility beta is less durable than policy-driven solar. Watch PLUG for hydrogen headline risk; keep position small.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rising middle-class disposable income in Indonesia continues to drive premiumization in FMCG categories, favoring brands with distribution reach in Tier-2/3 cities.
Digital commerce penetration is accelerating in consumer staples, creating structural winners among companies that have invested in direct-to-consumer and last-mile logistics.
Government subsidies and food-security policies are reshaping input costs for FMCG players, benefiting those with vertical integration or local sourcing advantages.
sectors.ai: Indonesia consumer/FMCG is in a watch phase with broad but uneven gains; the strongest moves are in small-cap names (COIN, JARR, BWPT) signaling speculative rotation rather than fundamental breadth. Position tactically in liquid large-caps with pricing power, and avoid chasing 20%+ single-day spikes. Watch for IDX momentum to confirm before adding; current signal favors holding existing exposure, not initiating new longs.
